routes.description: SIGNATURE / EXISTING SEALED CORRIDOR (Angra–Abraão, AGETRANSP T1 — economics sealed, unchanged). State ferry R$20.50 (up to 110 min) plus ~6 flexboats/day (~40 min, R$90–120). Haversine 11.4 nm; 13.0 nm kept per sealed route geometry threading the bay's island field.

SIGNATURE — The busiest Ilha Grande crossing: Conceição de Jacareí is the closest mainland pier to car-free Abraão, 15–20 min by flexboat, fares R$45–150 one-way depending on season/operator (typical R$60), embarkation tax R$10.30/leg. Haversine 6.5 nm + 0.5 nm threading the channel islets.

SIGNATURE — The Rio-side gateway: Barcas Rio state ferry Mangaratiba–Abraão (R$20.50, up to 110 min) plus flexboats (~40 min, 2x/day). Haversine 12.7 nm, effectively open-water. The natural first stop for traffic arriving from Rio de Janeiro down the BR-101.
Scheduled flexboat service departs Marina Porto Real at Conceição de Jacareí 4x/day for Abraão (15–20 min). Haversine 6.4 nm + 0.4 nm wrap out of the marina cove.
Scheduled lancha 3x/day (20–30 min) from Cais de Santa Luzia to Ilha Grande's west-coast pousada village. Haversine 8.7 nm + 0.8 nm rounding into the Enseada de Araçatiba.
Scheduled lancha (30–40 min, shared Araçatiba/Praia Vermelha service, from R$100). Haversine 9.4 nm + 0.6 nm coastal wrap along Ilha Grande's west shore.

The Lopes Mendes shuttle: taxi boats run Abraão–Pouso all day so visitors can walk the 20-min trail to Brazil's most-awarded beach (mapped as an OSM boat route). Haversine 1.9 nm + 0.6 nm wrapping the Ponta do Pouso headlands.

The classic half-day tour: daily lanchas and schooners from Abraão anchor at the turquoise Lagoa Azul snorkelling lagoon. Haversine 4.9 nm + 1.1 nm wrapping the north-coast headlands of the Enseada das Estrelas.
Lunch-stop leg of the north-coast tour circuit: Japariz beach restaurants receive the Lagoa Azul boats daily. Haversine 3.9 nm + 0.6 nm coastal wrap.
Abraão to the fjord-like Saco do Céu inlet — waterfront restaurants and the bay's signature sheltered anchorage, visited by daily tour boats. Haversine 3.4 nm + 0.6 nm entering the inlet.
Angra to Ilha da Gipóia's Praia do Dentista — the bay's boat-party beach, served by taxi boats and day charters from the town piers. Haversine 3.9 nm + 0.3 nm rounding Gipóia's north point.
Shortest hop on every Angra schooner circuit: the tourism pier to the white-sand islet of Cataguás. Haversine 1.95 nm.
Marina spur: BR Marinas Piratas (leisure-fleet base) direct to Abraão, skipping the town pier. Haversine 11.1 nm + 0.9 nm threading the island field.
Marina spur: Verolme's superyacht berths in Jacuecanga bay to the Angra passenger head. Haversine 3.9 nm + 0.5 nm rounding the Jacuecanga point.
Condominium feeder: Portogalo's marina to the Conceição de Jacareí flexboat head — a 5-minute water hop replacing the BR-101 shoulder. Haversine 2.4 nm.
West-bay link: Porto Frade's canal marina straight across to Ilha Grande's Araçatiba — today a private-boat-only run. Haversine 12.9 nm + 0.6 nm exiting the Frade canal.
West-shore marina hop between the Bracuhy and Frade communities. Haversine 2.9 nm + 0.3 nm clearing the river-mouth shallows.
Mainland coastal link between the two Ilha Grande gateways — today a 30-min drive on the BR-101. Haversine 7.8 nm + 0.5 nm coastal wrap along the Mangaratiba shore.

Cross-market Costa Verde heritage corridor: Angra to Paraty's colonial quay along the mainland shore. Haversine 25.2 nm + ~2.8 nm coastal wrap; 28 nm kept consistent with the Paraty package (paraty-brazil/route-inventory.json holds the mirror record to bp-dbf5302ce6).
